paper.title: Statistical modeling for selecting housekeeper genes
paper.citation: Szabo A, Perou CM, Karaca M, Perreard L, Palais R, Quackenbush JF, Bernard PS. Statistical modeling for selecting housekeeper genes. Genome Biology 5:R59 (2004); correction (author list) Genome Biology 9:405 (2008)
paper.license: BioMed Central open access (2004): verbatim copying and redistribution permitted in all media for any purpose, with the notice and the article's original URL

reml.what: Models fitted by REML (nlme's default for gls); natural logarithms throughout
reml.sensitivity: The paper names gls but not the criterion. Maximum likelihood does not converge for Model 1a on the breast data (nlme: false convergence), and for Model 2 it lowers the gene SDs by 6 to 16% (hypotheses.json).

vandesompele.what: Model 2's data are Vandesompele et al.'s Additional data file 1 as published (85 samples, 10 genes), tissue type from the sample name, values not rescaled
vandesompele.sensitivity: The paper cites the data but not the file. Rescaling the values within a panel changes only sample and tissue-by-gene effects, so Table 3 does not depend on it; the biases of Fig. 3 do, and come back as published from the values as they are.

fig_grid.what: Our figures are drawn on the published pixel grid: y from the tick marks and their printed values, one sample per grid line (Figs 1 and 2) or one bar per tissue tick (Fig. 3), markers cut from the published legend
fig_grid.sensitivity: Every calibration fits its ticks with a residual of 0 px. Nothing inside a panel is fitted; the residual misses are marker anchors (the down triangles sit about 2 px off) and the order in which overlapping markers are drawn.

items.label: Fig. 1a, raw expression of six genes in 80 breast tumours

assumptions.what: Samples ordered by the mean of their six log values (the caption's rule), ties kept in file order

items.label: Fig. 1b, the same on a log scale
Table 1, Model 1a standard deviations
Table 1, 95% confidence intervals

assumptions.what: Wald intervals on the log SDs from the numerical Hessian (Richardson extrapolation) of the REML likelihood
assumptions.sensitivity: The paper does not say how it computed the intervals. nlme's intervals() gives the same kind of interval from a coarser Hessian: across 24 equivalent parameterizations its bounds move by up to 0.005 (PSMC4's upper bound) and reach every printed bound.

cause.summary: The printed bounds are nlme's approximate intervals, whose numerical Hessian moves them in the third decimal with the order of the rows and the contrasts; across 24 such parameterizations nlme 3.1-164 reaches all 12 printed bounds. Ours, from an accurate Hessian, are within 0.002 of every printed bound.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The intervals are nlme's intervals(), which depend on the parameterization
hypotheses.test: intervals() for each gene as the varIdent reference, under treatment and sum contrasts and two row orders (24 fits)

hypotheses.hypothesis: The intervals come from maximum likelihood

items.label: Text: Model 1a has the best BIC of Models 1a, 1b and 1c
Text: microarray-selected genes against GAPD and ACTB, p = 0.0014

assumptions.what: The test: a likelihood ratio test of Model 1a against the model in which the four microarray-selected genes share one variance and GAPD and ACTB another (REML, 4 degrees of freedom)
assumptions.sensitivity: The paper does not name its test. This is the only one of four readings tried that gives 0.0014 (0.00139). The others: one variance for each group against one for all, p = 1.8e-9; a t test of the six SDs, p = 0.032; a t test of their logs, p = 0.049.

items.label: Table 2, best gene set of each size and the SD of its log geometric mean

assumptions.what: Variance of the log geometric mean of a set: sum of sigma_j^2 over the set divided by the squared set size
assumptions.sensitivity: The paper prints the divisor |S|, which gives none of rows 2 to 6 (row 2: 0.2430 against 0.1718); |S|^2, the variance of a mean, gives rows 1 to 5 as printed and row 6 one unit off. See text.set_variance_formula.

exceptions.evidence: The row prints SP3A1, a gene not in the study; the set is otherwise SF3A1's row (our set: MRPL19, PSMC4, PUM1, SF3A1).

cause.summary: Every set and five of the six SDs come back as printed; the six-gene SD is 0.151354, printed 0.1513, 0.000004 above the rounding boundary. Optimizer settings, the rounded SDs of Table 1 and truncation do not explain it.

hypotheses.hypothesis: An optimizer setting of the 2004 fit
hypotheses.test: 36 fits: each gene as the varIdent reference, two contrast codings, convergence tolerances 1e-6, 1e-4 and 1e-3

hypotheses.hypothesis: Computed from the rounded SDs of Table 1

hypotheses.test: Truncation gives row 6 0.1513 but rows 1, 3 and 4 as 0.2181, 0.1493 and 0.1489 against the printed 0.2182, 0.1494 and 0.1490

items.label: Methods: the printed variance of a set's log geometric mean (divided by the set size)

cause.summary: The formula divides by the set size where Table 2 divides by its square: on the paper's own Table 1 the best pair gives 0.1716 with the square (printed 0.1718) and 0.2426 with the size.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The divisor is the squared set size
hypotheses.test: Table 2 from our SDs with the squared set size and with the set size

items.label: Text: the four-gene set is lowest, three genes barely worse, two far worse
Text: the SDs of Table 2 are about the coefficients of variation on the original scale
Text: geNorm M-values give the same ranking except PUM1 and PSMC4, with MRPL19 and PSMC4 an unordered best pair

assumptions.what: geNorm's stepwise elimination (Vandesompele et al. 2002) on natural logs
assumptions.sensitivity: The log base scales every M by the same factor and does not change the ranking.

items.label: Methods: the printed bounds on the M-value under Model 1

cause.summary: The bounds print sigma_j^2 where sigma_j belongs (M is a mean of SDs): with sigma_j they hold for Model 1a's SDs, with sigma_j^2 they fail.

hypotheses.hypothesis: sigma_j^2 is a slip for sigma_j
hypotheses.test: Both forms against the M-values implied by Model 1a's SDs

items.label: Methods: the four candidate genes chosen from microarrays

cause.summary: A SAS selection of genes with 'a small range of expression' and 'the least variance' on 62 arrays (Perou et al. 2000 and cell lines), with no thresholds; it cannot be rerun as described, and its result (the four genes) is the paper's input, not one of its results.

items.label: Fig. 2, Vandesompele et al.'s data by tissue type

assumptions.what: Samples ordered within each tissue type by the mean of their ten log values; the wide FIB and NB panels have one and two empty grid lines at each edge
assumptions.sensitivity: The caption gives no order. Ordering by the mean of the raw values scores 58% (a near-miss control).

items.label: Table 3, Model 2 gene SDs
Table 3, Model 2 tissue multipliers

cause.summary: The same gap as the gene SDs (table3.sigma): our multipliers are 2.7 to 3.2% higher, so outside bone marrow the SDs varsigma_k sigma_j come within 2.7% of the printed products (bone marrow, where the multiplier is 1, carries the gene SDs' 2.1 to 5.2%).

items.label: Table 3, the order of the genes (GAPD lowest, then UBC, HPRT1, YWHAZ)
Methods: Model 2 has the best BIC of six variance structures
Text: the top five genes by mean geNorm rank over tissue types are Table 3's top five, in order

assumptions.what: geNorm ranks within each tissue type, the best pair both 1.5, averaged over the five tissue types

items.label: Table 4, minimax-MSE gene sets

assumptions.what: The bias of a gene set is the sum of its genes' tissue-specific biases (CG)_kj; its variance that of the log-average, varsigma_k^2 sum sigma_j^2 over the squared set size; MSE their sum, maximised over tissue types
assumptions.sensitivity: The paper describes the set MSE in words only. The mean of the biases (the bias of a log-average) gives 2 of the 10 printed sets; the sum gives all 10, and also gives the paper's ACTB plus TBP example on its own numbers (0.349; the mean gives 0.335).

assumptions.what: Row k is the best set with at most k genes
assumptions.sensitivity: The table's heading, 'Maximum number of members'; rows 3 to 5 and 7 to 9 repeat a set. Exactly k genes gives other sets at sizes 4, 5, 8 and 9.

cause.summary: Every set comes back; 5 of 10 MSEs are 0.001 off. They follow from Model 2's SDs (table3.sigma, open): with Table 3's printed SDs in place of ours, a sensitivity variant, 9 of 10 MSEs are as printed and the tenth (0.543 against 0.544) within Table 3's rounding.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The bias of a set is the mean of its genes' biases
The MSE differences come from Model 2's SDs
hypotheses.test: The same search with Table 3's printed SDs (sensitivity variant, not counted as agreement)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Model 2's SDs differ for a known reason
hypotheses.test: See table3.sigma: estimation method, model terms, log base and every single sample

assumptions.what: Bar width two thirds of the tick spacing and a 3 px outline
assumptions.sensitivity: lattice's default box.ratio (2); the R file of the figure (MOESM5) draws 9.99 pt bars every 14.985 pt.

items.label: Fig. 3, squared biases (bar heights in the publisher's R graphics file)

assumptions.what: Published heights read from the R PostScript of Fig. 3 (MOESM5.eps) at 0.01 pt, with the scale of the 0 and 8 tick labels (11.1175 pt per unit)
assumptions.sensitivity: The scale comes from two labels 88.9 pt apart, each placed at 0.01 pt: a relative uncertainty of 1.1e-4, which the tolerance includes.

items.label: Fig. 3, variances (bar heights in the publisher's R graphics file)

assumptions.what: Published heights read from the R PostScript of Fig. 3 (MOESM5.eps) at 0.01 pt, with the scale of the 0 and 8 tick labels
assumptions.sensitivity: The published variances equal Table 3's printed (varsigma_k sigma_j)^2 within its rounding (ACTB in bone marrow 0.2114 against 0.460^2 = 0.2116).

cause.summary: The variances are (varsigma_k sigma_j)^2 of Table 3, whose gap is open (table3.sigma): ours are 3 to 10% lower in bone marrow and within 5.2% elsewhere.

hypotheses.test: Published heights against Table 3's printed products

hypotheses.hypothesis: The figure's variances are maximum likelihood estimates
hypotheses.test: Model 2 by ML: its SDs are 6 to 16% below ours, further from the figure's

hypotheses.hypothesis: Model 2's SDs differ for a known reason

items.label: Text: ACTB plus TBP in pooled tissues, MSE 0.35 against individual MSEs above 6

assumptions.what: The set MSE of table4 (the biases of the set summed)
assumptions.sensitivity: On the paper's own numbers the sum gives 0.349 and the mean 0.335 (text.arithmetic); on ours 0.337 and 0.324.

cause.summary: Ours is 0.337, printed 0.35: the variance of the pair comes from Model 2's SDs (table3.sigma, open), and ours is 0.320 against 0.331 from Table 3's printed SDs, 3.3% low (ACTB's 5% low, TBP's on the mark). The paper's own Table 3 and Fig. 3 give 0.349. The individual MSEs (6.41 and 6.70) and the opposite signs come back.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The bias of the pair is the mean of the two biases
hypotheses.test: 0.324 on ours, 0.335 on the paper's numbers
The paper's Table 3 SDs with the published biases give 0.349

hypotheses.hypothesis: Model 2's SDs differ for a known reason

items.label: R package hkselect and its tutorial

status_note: the models rebuilt as the R package `hkselect`; Table 1's SDs, every gene set of Tables 2 and 4 and all 50 squared biases of Fig. 3 as printed; Figs 1-3 agree; Model 2's SDs (Table 3) 2 to 5% below the paper's for a reason not found
site_note: Table 1 and every gene set come back

page.lede: The authors fitted their models in R but never released the code. We rebuilt Models 1 and 2 from the paper's text as the R package hkselect and reran them on the paper's breast cancer data and on Vandesompele et al.'s data. Of {attempted} results we tried, {exact} came back exact, {agrees} agree, {partly} partly and {differs} differ.
page.tables_caption: Each table as printed and from our run. A value of ours matches when it rounds to the printed one.
page.items_caption: Every figure, table and claim of the paper, with its verdict from results.json.
page.claims_line: The main claims hold: MRPL19 is the best single gene and MRPL19, PUM1 and PSMC4 the chosen three-gene normaliser in breast cancer, and HPRT1, RPL13A and UBC the best small universal set. Of the results that do not match, Table 1's intervals differ in the third decimal as nlme's own do, two are slips in printed formulas, one is Table 2's last digit, and the rest follow from Model 2's SDs, which stay 2 to 5% below Table 3's for a reason we did not find.
came_back: All six standard deviations of Table 1 as printed, from the paper's own data and the nlme model it names.
Every best gene set, and five of the six standard deviations as printed.
p = 0.0014, from a likelihood ratio test the paper does not name.
All 50 squared biases within the resolution of the publisher's R graphics file.
Every minimax gene set, once the bias of a set is the sum of its genes' biases, as the paper's own ACTB and TBP example also needs.
buried: Model 2's standard deviations: ours stay 2 to 5% below Table 3, and no variant fit we tried reaches it.
Table 2's six-gene value, 0.000004 on the other side of a rounding boundary.
How the paper computed its confidence intervals; nlme's own spread covers every printed bound.
matched: Each value against the printed one at its printed precision; gene sets as sets.
Our points drawn on the published pixel grid with the published markers, scored both ways within 2 px, against wrong inputs and near misses.
The bars scored the same way, and every bar height read from the publisher's R graphics file.
Each claim checked first on the paper's own tables (8 of 8 hold there), then on our run.
page.closing: Szabo's housekeeper models came back as an R package.
